title: Starbucks (SBUX)’s New Chai Recipe has its Most Loyal Customers Revolting
summary: Starbucks faces backlash from loyal customers over its reformulated chai latte recipe, which was introduced in March with less sweetener and a new low-sugar base. While the company claims the change offers more customization, customers are petitioning for the original formula to return. Despite this, Starbucks' overall financial performance, including strong comparable sales and raised EPS guidance, suggests its broader turnaround remains on track, though managing customer loyalty amid menu changes will be crucial.

title: HCA Healthcare (HCA) Acquires a Healthcare College. Can Training Capacity Improve Staffing?
summary: HCA Healthcare (HCA) has acquired The College of Health Care Professions, a move aimed at improving staffing reliability and patient capacity by more closely aligning education with workforce needs. The acquisition builds on HCA's existing education network and prior collaborations with the college for training programs. While this strategy has the potential to reduce recruitment costs and improve staffing, its success hinges on student completion, successful hiring into HCA's network, and long-term retention of graduates.

title: Royalties at the border: Lessons from Colgate-Palmolive
summary: A recent Supreme Court decision regarding Colgate-Palmolive Philippines Inc. clarifies when royalties are included in the dutiable value of imported goods. Importers are advised to meticulously review their agreements and practices to differentiate royalties related to imported goods from other services to avoid potential customs issues.

title: National Protests at Elbit Systems
summary: The Palestine Solidarity Campaign is organizing national protests at Elbit Systems' facilities in Bristol and Shenstone on October 21, 2026. These protests aim to demand a comprehensive two-way arms embargo on Israel, citing Elbit Systems' role in manufacturing weapons used in the Gaza Strip and West Bank. The campaign calls for the British government to shut down Elbit Systems' sites and cease exporting weapons components to Israel.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Sued Again, This Time over How it Treats Pregnant Warehouse Workers
summary: Amazon is facing another lawsuit, a proposed nationwide class action, accusing it of systematically discriminating against pregnant warehouse workers by denying accommodations and firing those who miss work due to pregnancy-related issues. While Amazon asserts it approves over 99.9% of accommodation requests and has significant financial capacity to absorb potential costs, the lawsuit, along with ongoing cases in New Jersey and New York, poses reputational risks and could increase legal expenses, pushing the company to strengthen its workplace policies. Hedge fund interest in Amazon remains strong despite these legal challenges.

title: The AI Slowdown Trade Has Some Winners: CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Rally While Chips Fall
summary: Amid calls for a slowdown in AI development, a "risk-off" market move saw money shift from chip stocks to cybersecurity companies like Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD), which rallied significantly. Cybersecurity firms capitalized on this narrative, arguing that increased AI capabilities necessitate more robust security investments, although investors are cautioned to await actual demand data from upcoming earnings reports rather than relying solely on this sentiment-driven rally.

title: Claim Form Open: $250 million Apple iPhone false advertising class action settlement
summary: Apple has agreed to a $250 million class action settlement for consumers who purchased specific iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 models between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025. The lawsuit alleged that Apple failed to deliver certain Siri Apple Intelligence features as expected. Eligible class members can claim between $25 and $95 per device by submitting a claim form by December 21, 2026.

title: Oregon Woman’s Lawsuit Alleges Apple AirTag Enabled Stalking by Ex-Boyfriend
summary: An Oregon woman is suing Apple Inc., claiming her ex-boyfriend used an AirTag hidden in her car to stalk her. The lawsuit alleges that she never received an alert from Apple about the tracker and points to internal Apple data showing over 40,000 stalking reports involving AirTags between 2021 and 2024. Medford police have charged the former boyfriend with stalking using a GPS device.

title: Specialised Therapeutics expands Incyte partnership to Australia
summary: Specialised Therapeutics has expanded its partnership with Incyte Biosciences International to commercialize ruxolitinib cream (Opzelura) in Australia. Specialised Therapeutics will handle regulatory submissions, marketing, and distribution in Australia, while Incyte remains responsible for development and manufacturing.

title: L3Harris says digital KC-135 cockpit upgrade can keep U.S. tanker fleet mission-ready beyond 2050 and reduce sustainment costs
summary: L3Harris Technologies has proposed a digital avionics upgrade for the U.S. Air Force’s KC-135 aerial refueling fleet, aiming to extend its operational life beyond 2050. This modernization would replace obsolete flight deck instruments, reduce maintenance costs, and lower aircrew workload. The upgrade, based on government-owned architecture, is designed for quick fielding and future capability additions, ensuring the KC-135 remains central to global aerial refueling capacity.
